PERALES City Mayor Office of the City Mayor of Toledo, Cebu National Highway Toledo City, Cebu Dear Mayor Perales: This has reference to your letter dated 6 June 2024 requesting for this Department's legal opinion and guidance regarding the implementation and interpretation of Presidential Decree No. 449, also known as the Cockfighting Law of 1974, particularly on the following issues which are quoted in toto: "1. Presidential Decree No. 449 stipulates that only one cockpit may be established in each city or municipality. However, the also makes mention of the establishment of one cockpit in the poblaciön. This dual reference has led to varying interpretations. The primary points of clarification we seek are: a) Should the law be interpreted to mean a singular cockpit for the entire city, inclusive of its districts and the poblaciön? b) Alternatively, does the law allow one cockpit in the Poblacion in addition to one cockpit per district within the city? 2. The City of Toledo currently has an ordinance that designates seven (7) cockpits, with one located in each district. We seek clarification on whether the local legislation aligns with the limitations set by PD 449 regarding the number of cockpits permitted. Specifically, we request guidance on the following points: a) Does the existing city ordinance hold any legal validity if it exceeds the cockpit limitations set by PD 449? b) What measures should the city undertake to rectify this discrepancy? 3. Assuming the interpretation aligns with the national law's maximum of two cockpits per city, Toledo City presently has three (3) operational cockpits, we seek direction on the appropriate legal and administrative steps to address the situation. Specifically: "'Maüno. Mahusay at Maaasahan" runkline No. (02) 8876 3454

a) Are the established guidelines or precedents for determining which cockpits should continue operations and which should cease? b) What legal remedies or procedures should the city follow to ensure compliance while mitigating any adverse impact on stakeholders? Considering that the queries are interrelated, we deem it imperative to answer the same in one discussion. Please be informed that the Department had the occasion to answer similar queries in DILG Opinion No. 83, s. 2007, pertinent portions of which are quoted below: "xxxx please be informed that there is no exact definition of "POBLACION" under the Local Government Code, its implementing Rules and Regulations and other pertinent laws. However, in the case of People V. Moreno (34 OG 1769), POBLACION has been defined as the "center of municipality". It was also defined as a center of a municipality in the Philippines that is usually the barrio that gives the municipality its name and is the seat of the government [Webster's Third New International Dictionary]. With regard to the definition of "town district", we are quoting hereunder the opinion of Department of Justice No. 44 series of 1989 which was also quoted from the 2nd Indorsement dated June 24, 1984 of Deputy Minister Primicias Jr., of the Local Government Supervision, Ministry of Local Government: "There is no town district under the Local Government Code. Under Chapter 64, Art. VI of the Revised Administrative Code of 1917, however, Municipality may be subdivided into administrative district for purposed of supervision by Municipal Councilor. Said district may consist of one or more barrios or barangays." Under the same opinion, the Department of Justice (DOJ) held that the Sangguniang Panlungsod and Bayan are vested with the authority to regulate cockfighting and establishment of cockpits and hence, may provide by ordinance the districting. Prescinding from the said DOJ opinion, while there is no exact definition of a town or city district, the concerned city or municipality may, however be allowed to subdivide the said city into administrative district for purposes of supervision. Applying now the provisions of PD 1310, it is clear that the law authorizes the establishment of only two cockpits in the poblaciön and one in each district if the population concerned city is more than one hundred thousand. It is noted that the law uses the words "may be established'. The word "may" is ordinarily construed as directory or permissive (Crawford, statutory construction, 262, p-519). Thus, the establishment of more than one cockpit in the city with a population of over one hundred thousand is discretionary Page 2 of 3

with the licensing authority, provided that the maximum number of cockpits is, two in poblaciön and one each city/municipal district is not exceeded. Be that as it may, we would like to stress that under our settled jurisprudence, an ordinance which was already been approved enjoys presumption of validity, considering that the above-mentioned cockpit ordinance and its amendments had already gone through the substantial procedural process for its passage and approval as mandated under the Local Government Code, said ordinance now enjoys the presumption of validity unless later invalidated by the proper court of justice. However, no one is precluded to question the validity of the said ordinance in the proper court." As to the validity of the existing city ordinance regarding the establishment of cockpits, please be likewise informed that under Department Memorandum Order No. 2010-02, this Department as matter of policy shall not act on queries on presumptively valid acts (e.g. enacted ordinances) that enjoy presumption of regularity such as this instance. Any issues or questions thereon as to the substantive validity and enforceability of an ordinance should be threshed out by filing a special civil action for declaratory relief before the proper court in accordance with Sections I and 4, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court. 1 May we recommend, however, to reassess local regulations and policies related to cockpits. This may involve amending local ordinances to better align with PD 449 or to address any gaps in enforcement in the law. Lastly, we deem it proper to highlight the pronouncement of the Supreme Court in the case of Canet v. Decena2, to wit: "(i)t should, furthermore be borne in mind that cockfighting although authorized by law is still a form of gambling. Gambling is essentially antagonistic to the aims of enhancing national productivity and self- reliance. As has been previously said, a statue which authorizes amblin activit or business should be strictly. construed. and every reasonable doubt resolved so as to limit rather than expand the powers and rights claimed bv franchise holders under its authorit The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THO TY OF THE SE ARY: VI TOR R.
